thread:
anya: quick check — onboarding v0.9-k-dense. weights uploaded to s3://redwood-models/v0.9-k-dense/sha256:3f2a... can someone confirm tokenizer mapping? i'm seeing inconsistent EOS behavior when serving with current tokenizer.json :thinking:
mike: can you paste the exact path + sha? i want to validate the manifest against our model-registry scripts.
anya: path above, sha in the bucket metadata. manifest attached in the bucket too (manifest.json). also noticed tokenizer converts both ``<|endoftext|>`` and ``</s>`` to id 50256 in some convert_paths — might be a multer issue.
val: hmm that sounds like 2 tokenizer vocab variants were merged. quick test:
```
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('hello</s>').ids, t.encode('hello<|endoftext|>').ids)"
```
val: on my end the ids differ. can you `sha256sum tokenizer.json` and confirm? :mag:
anya: sha256 is 6a8b... matches the bucket file. weird. infra-bot, config-validator is failing when i try to register the model for serving — error about max_request_tokens > model_max_tokens.
infra-bot: validation error for model v0.9-k-dense: 
```
ERROR: invalid_config: request_max_tokens (2048) > model.max_seq_len (1024)
at register_model (model_registry.py:213)
```
sam: that's the immediate blocker. either we set a lower request_max_tokens or the model.max_seq_len in the model config. what's the real model context length?
anya: upstream model was trained with 1024. i wrongly used our default 2048 in the serving config. i can lower request_max_tokens. any recommandations for continuous batching knobs for this model? target p50 latency ~60ms.
mike: for 1024 model and medium token mix i'd start with:
```
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_latency_ms: 20
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096   # keep small to avoid long tails
  max_concurrent_batches: 4
  token_bucket_size: 8192
```
:thumbsup:
val: also enable prefix_kv_cache with TTL = 600 for chat workloads; set cache.policy = "prefix_v1" — that avoids caching whole responses. for safety set cache.max_prefix_tokens = 256.
lee: note that `max_tokens_per_batch` must be consistent with `request_max_tokens` * concurrent clients — otherwise scheduler will starve. reduce `request_max_tokens` to 768 if you want tight p50 targets.
anya: ok changing request_max_tokens->768, continuous knobs per mike, cache TTL 600 and max_prefix_tokens 256. updating the model config now.
infra-bot: suggested config diffs applied to staging model entry. run `rctl validate --model v0.9-k-dense --env staging` to check.
mike: small follow-up: set scheduler.queue_weights: {interactive: 3, batch:1} if you'll have mixed traffic. keeps interactive short latency.
val: tokenizer mismatch still worrying. if tokenizer.json collides between training and conversion, we should add a pre-start hook to normalize EOS tokens: replace `</s>` with `<|endoftext|>` mapping and regenerate merges. will open a tiny PR for a normalizer script.
anya: thanks — i'll hold deploy until CI + validator green. will ping when i flip to dedicated pool. :wave:
lee: lgtm — ping me if staging latencies spike after enabling continuous batching.
anya: noted, TY all.
